prompt: Write `fn fizzbuzz(n: Int) -> Text`: "FizzBuzz" if n is divisible by 15, "Fizz" if by 3, "Buzz" if by 5, otherwise the number as text (e.g. "7"). n >= 1 (state that as a precondition).
Write `fn reverse_words(t: Text) -> Text`: words are separated by single spaces; return the words in reverse order, joined by single spaces. "a bb c" -> "c bb a". An empty text gives an empty text.

Write `fn is_palindrome(t: Text) -> Bool`: true if t reads the same forwards and backwards when you ignore case and keep only ASCII letters and digits. "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" -> true; "abc" -> false; "" -> true. Text is ASCII.
hidden: is_palindrome("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama") == true

prompt: Write `fn mean(xs: List[Float]) -> Opt[Float]`: the arithmetic mean, or none for an empty list.
Write `fn rle(t: Text) -> Text`: run-length encoding of an ASCII text: each run of the same character becomes the character followed by the run length. "aaabcc" -> "a3b1c2". "" -> "".

Write `fn balanced(t: Text) -> Bool`: true if the brackets ( ) [ ] { } in t are balanced and properly nested; all other characters are ignored. "a(b[c]{d})" -> true, "(]" -> false, "((" -> false, "" -> true.

Write `fn rpn(t: Text) -> Opt[Int]`: evaluate a reverse-Polish expression of integers and the operators + - * separated by single spaces. "3 4 + 2 *" -> some(14). Return none if the expression is malformed (unknown token, not enough operands, or not exactly one value left at the end). Numbers may be negative like "-5".

Define `record Item { name: Text, price: Int, qty: Int }` (price in cents). Write `fn total(items: List[Item]) -> Int` (sum of price*qty) and `fn priciest(items: List[Item]) -> Opt[Text]` (name of the item with the highest price; on a tie, the first one; none for an empty list).
